_note: Finnish interface text. Register: sinä (2nd person singular) where a person has to be addressed at all, and Finnish's ordinary impersonal/passive elsewhere; buttons and commands are imperative singular (Tallenna, Vie, Tuo, Sulje, Peruuta, Aloita). Terms: arkki = sheet, sivu = face, kortti = card, paperi = paper/page size, osio = section, palsta = column, rivi = row/item/entry, kenttä = field, kirjasin = typeface, kirjasinkoko = type size, ääntämisohje = respelling, latinaistus = romanisation, käännös = gloss, ladonta = typesetting (deliberately not taitto, which is needed for the fold finishing), taitto = fold, musteensäästö = low ink, mustavalko = mono. Keys where a judgement call was made and a fluent speaker should confirm: format.theme.accessible ("Värivarma", a coinage on the pattern of Swedish "Färgsäker" and German "Farbsicher"; the theme id is cvd-safe, so it is about colour-vision deficiency rather than accessibility in general -- if the broader reading is meant, "Saavutettava" would be safer). format.theme.reference ("Viite" is thin as a theme name; "Hakukortti" would be more concrete but longer). field.script ("Alkuperäinen kirjoitus", after German "Originalschrift"; Finnish cannot say "their script" the way Swedish and Czech can, because a third-person possessive in a UI label reads oddly -- the terser "Kirjoitus" is the alternative). format.textPadding and format.paddingTitle ("reunatila": Finnish has no settled print word for padding as distinct from marginaali and riviväli, so this is transparent rather than standard). format.typeface.serif and .sans ("Antiikva" and "Groteski" are the correct Finnish print terms but are less familiar to non-typographers than the English words). format.priority together with tree.importanceTitle (English separates Priority from Importance; Finnish uses one root, so the selector is "Tärkeystaso" and the per-row value "Tärkeys"). studio.pair ("{target} - {source}": the names arrive uninflected, so no Finnish case ending can be attached and a plain dash is used for the pair). drill.heading, drill.open, drill.again ("Testi" for Quiz; "kysely" would mean a survey and "visa" a game show). ornament.laurel ("Laakerikäsikirjoitus", a literal compound -- there is no established Finnish name for that ornament style). roman.mccune (written with a hyphen, "McCune-Reischauer", because the catalogue is kept to ASCII plus ä ö; the usual typography has an en dash). Characters: the only Finnish letters beyond ASCII are ä and ö; · … — ← → ⊞ × are carried over unchanged from en.json as interface furniture. Percentages and units are spaced as Finnish orthography requires (5 %, 12 pt, 8.5 in).
